speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help narrow down the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy secondary to Anabolic Steroid Abuse (Parsley Syndrome).

The patient's history of anabolic steroid use, combined with progressive distal weakness, sensory loss, weight loss, and chronic alcohol consumption, is highly suggestive of steroid-induced brachial plexopathy, likely exacerbated by alcoholic neuropathy and potential malignancy. I will now request imaging to confirm the extent of nerve and muscle involvement.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Shoulder and Arm with contrast.
